chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz al-Abdi, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Humran, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), saying to him, 'When is it obligatory upon the boy that he should be seized with the complete Penalties (Hudud), and for it to be established upon him and for him to be seized by it?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When the orphan-hood exits from him, and he attains realisation (adراك).' I said, 'So for that is a Penalty (Hadd) to be recognised by?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When he bed-wets (ihtalam), or reaches fifteen years of age, or grows hair (ash'ara), or grows pubic hair (anbata) before that, the complete Penalties would be established upon him, and he would be seized by it, and it would be taken for him.' I said, 'So, for the girl, when would the complete Penalties be Obligated upon her, and these would be taken for her, and she would be seized by it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The girl is not like the boy. The girl, when she gets married and copulated with (dakhila biha), and for her are nine years, the orphan-hood goes away from her, and her wealth is handed over to her, and her instructions are allowed with regards to the buying and the selling, and the complete Penalties would be established upon her, and she would be seized by it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And the boy, his instructions are not allowed with regards to the buying and the selling, and he does not come out from the orphan-hood until he reaches fifteen years of age, or bed-wets, or grows hair, or grows pubic hair before that.'
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of maturity for boys and girls regarding the obligation of Islamic legal penalties (Hudud)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the distinct criteria for full legal accountability (bulugh) in Shia jurisprudence, highlighting a nuanced difference between genders where girls attain maturity upon marriage and consummation at age nine, while boys require physical signs of puberty or reaching fifteen. Scholars note this reflects the practical application of 'ahl al-hudud' (those subject to penalties), linking biological maturity with legal capacity for financial transactions and criminal liability. The distinction underscores the Shia view that marriage confers immediate legal majority to girls, contrasting with the boy's continued status as an orphan under guardianship until physical maturity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al Abady, from Hamza Bin Humran, from Humran who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws saying to himasws, ‘When is it Obligatory upon the boy that he should be seized with the complete Penalties, and for it to be established upon him and for him to be seized by it?’ So heasws said: ‘When the orphan-hood exits from him, and he attains realisation’. I said, ‘So for that is a Penalty (Hadd) to be recognised by?’ So heasws said: ‘When he bed-wets, or reaches fifteen years of age, or becomes aware, or grows (pubic hair) before that, the complete Penalties would be established upon him, and he would be seized by it, and it would be taken for him’. I said, ‘So, for the girl, when would the complete Penalties be Obligated upon her, and these would be taken for her, and she would be seized by it?’ Heasws said: ‘The girl is not like the boy. The girl, when she gets married and copulated with, and for her are nine years, the orphan-hood goes away from her, and her wealth is handed over to her, and her instructions are allowed with regards to the buying and the selling, and the complete Penalties would be established upon her, and she would be seized by it. And the boy, his instructions are not allowed with regards to the buying and the selling, and he does not come out from the orphan-hood until he reaches fifteen years of age, or bed-wets, or becomes aware, or grows (pubic hair) before that’.
